title: The three /invoke handlers share one trace_ids input contract
answers: why does issues/invoke accept an empty trace_ids list
non-string trace_ids returns 500 on scorer invoke
how should trace_ids be validated and deduplicated in invoke handlers
consistent trace_ids validation across invoke endpoints
body:
Convention: scorer/invoke, issues/invoke and genai/evaluate/invoke all validate trace_ids the same way, so keep them in sync.
Schema: [_assert_required, _assert_array, _assert_item_type_string]. Non-string items return 400 before the store is consulted.
Empty list: reject with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. Previously issues/invoke submitted a no-op run and job for [].
Dedupe: list(dict.fromkeys(trace_ids)) before any lookup or submission, preserving order.
applies: Any new or edited handler that takes a trace_ids list under the /invoke routes.
says: Submitting an empty trace list to issue detection creates an unnecessary background job.
Scorer invocation crashes with server errors when trace entries are not strings.
Ensure consistent trace input validation across all evaluation invoke endpoints.
Deduplicate repeated trace selections while preserving order when running evaluations.
search: The scorer/invoke, issues/invoke, and genai/evaluate/invoke handlers in mlflow/server/handlers.py share a unified trace_ids input validation and deduplication contract. Handlers require an array of strings, returning 400 for non-string items and INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE for empty lists. Trace IDs must be deduplicated using list(dict.fromkeys(trace_ids)) to preserve order before lookup or submission.
